goHarness: isolated resource ownership, concurrent completion observer and final accounting
notes: One loop: decision + impression + click + conversion (4 HTTP calls, 3 Kafka events). All users match a 3-advertiser first-price auction at 5 fen. Fresh request IDs.

k6 acceptance latency differs from committed statistical completion. Observer queries every 250ms during load; completion includes polling/query/scheduling delay and uses a client timestamp embedded in requestId on the same WSL host.
Three complete warmup flows per stage are excluded from measured rates/latencies, included in campaign money and metric checks. 1000 persisted profiles are prewarmed; no temporary-profile bypass.
Fresh campaigns per stage preserve frequency/budget headroom. Never reset financial state during load; only own profile cache values evicted between stages. Old stage data remains in isolated DB.
No source, relay batch size/poll period, worker count, connection pool, or timeout tuning during search. Colocated load generator/API/MySQL/Redis/Kafka share hardware; not production maximum.
No-Ad is a failure, not a fast successful flow. All accepted events must commit, publish, process and reconcile; Kafka broker lag must be zero after drain. Failed stages retained.
Only report a rate after three 60s confirmations by default. Probe failures are expected data; no within-stage automatic retry hides HTTP errors.
scenario: k6 fixed-arrival-rate full Kafka business capacity search
timingBoundary: HTTP acceptance and committed statistical visibility are measured separately
